**Generated by:** Claude (Research & Theoretical Architect)
**Date:** 2026-09-10
**For:** Antigravity (Software Engineer Architect)
**Supersedes:** the earlier 2026-09-10 production-readiness plan, which is complete.

**Research basis:**
- `05 - Claude Notes/2026-09-10 - Model Training Plan and Project Roadmap.md`
- `05 - Claude Notes/2026-09-10 - Raspberry Pi Deployment Architecture and Runbook.md`
- `02 - Code Review/2026-09-10 - Live Integration Bring-Up - Sampling Rate and Latency Defects.md`

## Context

The acquisition chain is live on real sensor data and validated with a real finger.
The system is integration-ready. Two things are now true that shape this plan:

1. **Model training is owned by a teammate, in Google Colab.** Do not build a local
   training pipeline, do not install CUDA, do not train on the Pi. Our deliverable is
   the *contract* around training, so the returned weights drop into the deployed NumPy
   forward pass unchanged.
2. **The system can still present untrained output as if it were diagnostic.** That is
   the highest-value thing to fix while the model is being trained elsewhere.

Read the roadmap note before starting — Decisions 1–3 there explain why DeepBeat is the
corpus, why the data is resampled to 100 Hz rather than the pipeline being changed, and
why the deliverable is a weights file rather than a Keras or TFLite model.

---

## 1. Honesty guards (do these first — they are small and they matter most)

- [ ] `03 - ML/model/inference_model.py` currently falls back to seeded random He
      initialisation when no trained weights exist, which is precisely why an untrained
      model looked operational for a week. Add explicit weight loading from an `.npz`,
      and record on the instance whether real weights were loaded.
- [ ] Propagate that state: every telemetry payload from `runner.py` gains
      `model_trained: true|false`.
- [ ] The dashboard must render an unmistakable, persistent banner whenever
      `model_trained` is false — the AF probability and the Grad-CAM strip are not
      diagnostic in that state and must be labelled as such. Reuse the pattern already
      built for `ENABLE_SIMULATION`.
- [ ] Do **not** hide or suppress the AF output — it is still needed to prove the
      pipeline works. Label it, do not remove it.

## 2. Training handoff artefacts (write these, hand them over, do not run them)

Target `03 - ML/training/` — a new directory, kept separate from the edge runtime so
nothing here ever ships to the Pi.

- [ ] `preprocess_deepbeat.py` — reads `03 - ML/data/deepbeat/*.npz`, and:
      - extracts `signal.npy` from the archive and memory-maps it (`mmap_mode='r'`);
        the members are stored uncompressed, so this works and avoids an 18 GB read
      - resamples 32 Hz → 100 Hz (`scipy.signal.resample_poly`, up=25, down=8)
      - slices each 25 s segment into 10 s / 1000-sample windows
      - applies the same detrend → Butterworth 0.5–5 Hz → z-score chain as
        `03 - ML/signal_processing/`, imported from there rather than reimplemented, so
        training and inference cannot drift apart
      - splits **by subject**, never by window — `parameters.npy` carries the subject
        identifiers; verify which column before relying on it
      - writes `float32` shards small enough to upload to Google Drive
      - prints class balance per split
- [ ] `keras_model.py` — the architecture from `ANTIGRAVITY.md` §4.3, exactly:
      `Conv1D(32,5,same)+ReLU+MaxPool(2)` → `Conv1D(64,3,same)+ReLU+MaxPool(2)` →
      `Flatten` → `Dense(64,ReLU)` → `Dropout(0.5)` → `Dense(1,sigmoid)`;
      BCE loss, Adam(1e-3), early stopping on validation loss.
- [ ] `export_weights.py` — writes a `.npz` of named arrays in the exact layout
      `inference_model.py` expects. Document the naming and the expected kernel
      orientation in a docstring; this is the interface.
- [ ] `verify_equivalence.py` — loads an exported `.npz` into the NumPy model, runs
      identical input through both implementations, asserts agreement within
      floating-point tolerance, and exits non-zero on failure. **This is the acceptance
      test for anything returned from Colab.** Padding, channel order and kernel
      orientation are the usual failure points, and a mismatch produces confident wrong
      predictions with no error raised.
- [ ] `03 - ML/training/README.md` — a short Colab runbook: what to upload, what to run,
      what to send back, and the note that checkpoints belong on Drive because Colab
      sessions expire.

## 3. Calibrate the SQI gate against ground truth

- [ ] The deployed `MIN_SQI_SCORE = 0.7` was picked by eye during bring-up. DeepBeat's
      `qa_label` is a 3-class human-labelled signal-quality ground truth over the same
      signal type — use it to choose a defensible threshold and report the
      sensitivity/specificity of the gate itself.
- [ ] Same for `CONTACT_IR_THRESHOLD = 50000`, inherited from the legacy sketch.
      Confirm it against real contact/no-contact captures.
- [ ] Record the chosen values and their justification in an ADR.

## 4. Data cleanup (order matters — get it wrong and the edge service will not start)

- [ ] Create a real patient through the dashboard.
- [ ] Repoint `TARGET_PATIENT_ID` in `/home/ranilo/.config/arrhythmia/edge.env` at it.
- [ ] Only then purge: the 3 seeded patients, the 224 events (4 synthetic plus ~220
      from bring-up noise, all with `af_detected=1` from the untrained model), **and the
      two compromised `users` rows** — `03 - ML/scripts/purge_synthetic_data.py` does
      not currently touch the `users` table and must be extended.
- [ ] The SHA-256 chain cannot be patched after deletion; reinitialise from genesis and
      re-verify via `/api/events/verify/chain`.
- [ ] Surface the exact commands for review before running anything against the live
      database.

## 5. Documentation corrections

- [ ] `ANTIGRAVITY.md` §5: the Performance Efficiency row claims "inference ~13.08 ms".
      That was measured on synthetic data and is stale. The real figure is 27.7–42.1 ms
      and the 25 ms budget is **breached on every window**. Correct it and mark the
      budget as not met.
- [ ] `ANTIGRAVITY.md` §4.3 and Chapter 2 both name the **MIMIC PERform AF Dataset**,
      but the corpus actually downloaded and to be trained on is **DeepBeat**
      (Torres-Soto & Ashley 2020, Synapse `syn22006404`). Flag this for the team — the
      thesis text has to be corrected either way, and it is not Antigravity's call to
      pick. Do not silently change Chapter 2.
- [ ] Update the Functional Suitability row to state plainly that sensitivity,
      specificity and accuracy are **not yet measurable** because the model is untrained.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **Training the model.** A teammate does this in Colab. No local training pipeline, no
  CUDA install, no training on the Pi.
- Hyperledger Fabric sync. Still deferred.
- Rotating or removing the login credentials — the owner asked that these be left alone
  for now. They are documented in the gitignored `CREDENTIALS.md`.
- Any redesign of the dashboard's visual language.

## Notes for Antigravity

Section 1 is the priority: it is perhaps forty lines of code and it closes the gap
that let untrained output look diagnostic. Section 2 is the largest piece of work but
is pure offline tooling with no deployment risk. Sections 3–5 can proceed in any order.

The system is currently live and working. Anything touching `03 - ML/edge_inference/`,
the firmware, or the telemetry contract must be verified against the running Pi — see
the runbook for the remote flashing procedure and the validity-gating contract that
must not regress.
